go_dev_text: New customers choose: their own device (about 15 %, router freedom), or renting or buying - whatever is cheaper for them over 120 days. Rented devices stay yours: when one breaks you replace it, when a customer leaves it comes back. Market prices: rent about {0} a day, buy about $120-$180.

go_flt_installs_text: Fiber always needs a technician at the customer's, coax a quarter of the time. An appointment missed by more than 24 hours costs compensation, and some customers cancel.

go_flt_text: Free technicians take the most urgent fault. A fault that is not fixed within two days costs compensation from the third day ($5 or 10 % of the monthly price per customer and day, from the 5th day $10 or 20 %). You can drive there yourself and repair it on site.
go_found_package: The start: a CMTS for DOCSIS 3.0 at the headend, 25 cable modems and three tariffs to begin with (you can change them). Prices are per day, like rent and wages in the game. The first technician's van can be leased in the Staff tab.
go_found_text: Buy bandwidth, connect the city's buildings and sell internet, TV and phone lines - against Skyline Cable, the city's old cable company. You start small with DOCSIS 3.0; DOCSIS 3.1 and fiber to the home (XGS-PON) come later.

go_net_transit_text: You buy a fixed amount from a carrier. The bigger, the cheaper per Mbit/s. Billing as with the 95th percentile: the busiest hour of the day does not count; above the booked amount it costs 1.5 times as much. Beyond twice the amount the line is full and everybody slows down.

Cheaper draws more customers, much dearer makes them leave. A minimum term lowers cancellations but puts a few people off. Over 500 Mbit/s only with DOCSIS 3.1.
go_tv_paytv_text: Wholesale contracts with Pay-TV providers: they charge you per subscriber and day (some a minimum per day), you set the price and bill your customers. Pay-TV needs the CA system (encryption) and a smartcard per subscription (Devices tab).

Coax customers who cancel keep the signal until their tap is disconnected.

go_permit_text: Every building has a contract with its owner for two game years. Renew it before it ends - or there is a tender, and with a poor reputation Skyline Cable takes the building and its customers. Field sales make renewing cheaper and tenders easier to win.
go_role_master_text: One per neighbourhood: plans and looks after the network there - 40 % fewer coax faults, network faults need less work, and building and upgrades take the normal time (twice as long without a network master). Needs a workplace and a car, works 8-16.
go_role_sales_text: Goes from door to door in your buildings: where they were, more people sign that day. Negotiates the permission contracts with the owners - renewing costs 30 % less, and tenders are won more often. Needs a car.
go_role_service_text: Takes new orders (porting included) and answers the calls - during outages many customers call. Unanswered calls cost reputation. Needs a workplace.
go_role_support_text: Diagnoses faults from the desk: a broken device is often fixed remotely, the rest needs less work on site; Wi-Fi problems are solved by remote access (without support a technician has to drive there). Needs a workplace.
go_role_switch_text: Switches the taps of coax customers on and off (DOCSIS). Without switching staff the technicians do it besides their work. Needs a van.
go_role_tech_text: Fixes faults and keeps the appointments at the customers'. Needs a van.

Too few people show up here first: faults stay open (technicians), taps wait (switching staff), calls go unanswered and orders pile up (customer service). Ways out: hire (Staff tab shows the need per role), contractors for the jobs that wait, overtime for a few days.

go_rival_text: The city's old cable company. At first it has every household, and it fights back where you take its customers: it cuts its prices, tries to win customers back with switching bonuses, upgrades its network, signs exclusive contracts with the owners of buildings you have not connected yet and bids in every tender. On a day its own network fails, many of its customers look for someone else. How hard it fights follows the game's setting for rivals and the mod option.
go_steps_build: Connect a few big buildings near the headend (tab Buildings) - each neighbourhood first needs a node.
go_steps_customers: The first customers sign: until you have staff for it, you take the orders yourself between 8 and 20 o'clock and switch the connections on.
go_steps_hire: Hire a technician or switching staff (tab Staff) - they switch on the new customers in the buildings.

help_goingonline:businesstype_cablecente:
# Offices, hubs and customer centers

Every neighbourhood needs **an office of yours and a customer center** - otherwise nobody new signs there, no new building can be connected, and the customers there cancel little by little.

- The **headend** (your first office) has the satellite TV, the internet line, telephony and Pay-TV for the whole city.
- An **office in another neighbourhood** becomes a **hub** once you build its **feeder fibre** from the headend (Network tab) and a CMTS stands there: its CMTS and OLT serve the nodes and customers of that neighbourhood, its staff work there. A neighbourhood without a hub of its own hangs on the headend.
- A **ring** - a second way for the fibre, to another hub or separately to the headend - keeps a hub running when an excavator cuts its feeder; without it the whole neighbourhood is off until the splice crew is done.
- A **customer center** (a shop, *Cable customer center*) has the customer service and the devices. People of the neighbourhood come in while it is open: they look at the **device table** (Going Online's, from the furniture stores), sit down on the **waiting places** (the game's waiting room chairs, sofas or benches), watch the **television** - every TV there shows your company's spot - and go to a **customer desk** (Going Online's customer center workplace with someone on shift). New customers of the neighbourhood pick their devices up there - no parcel to pay for.

**Who serves how many:** a technician 400 customers, switching staff 800 coax customers, customer service 500 customers - each in the neighbourhood of their office or customer center. A network master leads up to 10 people in the field; beyond that they work slower. The Staff tab shows it per neighbourhood.

**Power and monitoring:** now and then the city's power fails in a neighbourhood. Batteries in the nodes' power supplies (Network tab, per neighbourhood) bridge two hours; a **UPS** keeps an office running for an hour, a **generator** as long as the cut lasts - without them a dark hub takes its neighbourhood down, the dark headend the whole city. The **network monitoring** (Network tab, a licence per day) finds faults before customers call, while a network master is on duty and a control room workplace stands in an office.

A provider from before Going Online 0.8 keeps the old rules for 10 days after the update.
help_goingonline:businesstype_cableprovi:
# Founding a cable provider

The order: **first an office as the headend, then a customer center in a shop** - both must stand before the first customers sign.

1. Rent or buy an **office**. Open it in **BizMan**, *Start new business*, choose **Cable provider**, type the company's name and start the business - like every office business it needs the course **Office Businesses** of the Manhattan Business School. Going Online founds the provider with it: this office is the **headend**. The app is in the phone and in the full menu (Shift+F12).
2. Set the office up like every office business: a **CMTS** (without it the network does not run), Going Online's **technical workplace** (a computer - on a desk, with a chair), **toilets** (one per 100 m²) and **sinks** (one per 200 m²), up to four each - BizMan lists them under the business's requirements, and the staff work only when all are there. Hire a cable technician at **Anderson Recruitment Corp.** and give them a shift at the workplace.
3. Rent a **shop** in the same neighbourhood and found **Cable customer center** there in BizMan. Set up Going Online's **customer center workplace** (the customer desk) and assign customer service; the devices for new customers lie on storage shelves there.
4. Connect the first buildings in the app's *Buildings* tab.

A customer center alone founds nothing - the provider always begins with its office. More neighbourhoods: see *Offices, hubs and customer centers*.
help_goingonline_help_customers_content:
# Tariffs and customers

In the app's *Tariffs* tab you set the speeds, prices, TV and phone of your tariffs and the fees (connection, move, fault service). People compare them with the competitor's prices. Subscriptions, Pay-TV packages and device rent are the **Cable provider** business's own sales: BizMan's reports show them, and the game pays them at midnight.

Satisfied customers stay and tell others; faults, long waits, unfriendly technicians and missed appointments drive them away.
help_goingonline_help_devices_content:
# Devices and suppliers

Cable modems (DOCSIS 3.0 and 3.1), ONTs for fiber, IPTV set-top boxes and Pay-TV smartcards are **goods**. **Every wholesaler** of the city has them on its shelves: buy the boxes there and put them on a **storage shelf** in the office - what lies there is the stock, a new customer's device comes from there. The *Devices* page names the wholesaler nearest to the headend. With Going Public Server a wholesaler also delivers them: call it (Contacts), start a delivery contract for the cable provider and set the amounts in BizMan (*Deliveries*) - they come at 8 o'clock onto the storage shelves in the office.

Later, with a **headquarters**, a **purchasing agent** and a **warehouse**, an **importer** with electronics delivers them too (an import plan, as for every import); devices in your own warehouses count as stock as well.

Devices customers give back are refurbished and go out first. When the stock is empty, new customers wait (up to three days) and the technicians buy a device in a hurry for a repair - at one and a half times the price.
help_goingonline_help_remove_content:
# Removing the mod

A save with a cable provider needs this mod. Before you remove it, open the app's *Finance* tab and press **Prepare the removal**, then save the game. The cable provider becomes an empty office (a headend of 0.6 a warehouse), a customer center an empty building, the equipment and workplaces the game's furniture they were made from; devices in storage are gone; your staff keep working with the game's jobs.
help_goingonline_help_rival_content:
# The competitor

**Skyline Cable** is the city's old cable company. Where you take its customers it fights back: price cuts, switching bonuses, network upgrades, exclusive contracts with building owners and bids in the tenders for permission contracts. How hard it fights follows the game's rivals setting and the mod option *Competition*.
help_goingonline_help_staff_content:
# Staff

Your staff are the game's employees, and the jobs come with the **workplaces**: the recruitment agencies offer the cable provider exactly the jobs whose workplaces stand in its office.
- Going Online's **technical workplace**: cable technicians, switching staff, network masters;
- the **customer center workplace**: customer service, technical support, field sales, network masters.

The office furniture stores sell both. Cable technicians, switching staff and customer service are at **Anderson Recruitment Corp.**, network masters, field sales and technical support at **City Workforce Inc.**

Network masters can also be hired for your **headquarters**: they work at its computers and get a shift there.

The workplaces are computers: each needs a desk and a chair, else nobody works there - as in every office of the game. Everyone gets a **shift** at a workplace in BizMan (*Schedule*) - one person per workplace and shift. The game pays the wages. Technicians and switching staff also need a van at the office, network masters and field sales any vehicle (park it there, within 80 m, or lease one in the app). Each shift gets a free vehicle by itself; in BizMan's tab *Fleet* a vehicle can also be assigned to one person (Going Public Server).

How friendly someone is with customers follows their customer-service skill; complaints and a customer-care training are in the app.

help_gps_help_it_content:
# IT firm

Rent an **office** and found in BizMan one of three businesses: **IT Support**, **Software Development** or **Cloud Services**.

- Hire the staff at **City Workforce Inc.**: IT support, software developers or cloud engineers.
- Give each of them an **IT workplace** (office furniture store) and a shift in BizMan.
- **Servers** must stand in the office: IT support needs a blade server per four workplaces, software development a rack server per four, cloud services a rack per four and a mainframe per twelve. Short of servers the staff work at a third. Servers cost power every day: blade 40 $, rack 80 $, mainframe 160 $.
- Each employee bills an hour when a client needs it - more with skill and good spirits, most in office hours, fewer at a high price. Set the hourly price in BizMan (IT support 55 $, software 85 $, cloud 110 $ is the market's price).
help_gps_help_cleaning_content:
# Cleaning company

Rent an **office** and found a **Cleaning Company** in BizMan.

- Hire **cleaners** at Anderson Recruitment Corp. and **crew leads** at City Workforce Inc.; each needs a **cleaning cart** (their workplace, office furniture store) and a shift. Evenings and nights pay best.
- The crews clean about 120 m² an hour each. They first clean **your own other businesses** - their dirt goes away, the dirtiest first - then clients of the city pay by the hour.
- A **floor scrubber** makes a crew a fifth faster, a **carpet extractor** a tenth, a **window kit** a twentieth (one piece per person counts); a crew lead on shift adds a tenth.
- Cleaning supplies cost about 1.50 $ per person and hour. Set the hourly price in BizMan (market: 35 $).
help_gps_help_laundromat_content:
# Laundromat

Rent a **shop** and found a **Laundromat** in BizMan.

- Set up **washers** and **dryers** from the appliance store: a washer takes a load an hour (8 kg one, 12 kg one and a half, the 27 kg giant three), a dryer one (15 kg) or two (30 kg).
- People of the neighbourhood come - more where many pass by, most in the evening, fewer at high prices. Most loads go into a dryer afterwards.
- With an **attendant** (customer service, Anderson Recruitment Corp.) on shift, some leave their laundry for **wash and fold**; **folding tables** make it faster. A **bill changer** brings a few more people.
- Water, power and detergent cost about 0.80 $ a load. Prices in BizMan (market: wash 4 $, dry 3 $, wash and fold 18 $).

help_goingonline_help_offices_content:
# Offices, hubs and customer centers

Every neighbourhood needs **an office of yours and a customer center** - otherwise nobody new signs there, no new building can be connected, and the customers there cancel little by little.

- The **headend** (your first office) has the satellite TV, the internet line, telephony and Pay-TV for the whole city.
- An **office in another neighbourhood** becomes a **hub** once you build its **feeder fibre** from the headend (Network tab) and a CMTS stands there: its CMTS and OLT serve the nodes and customers of that neighbourhood, its staff work there. A neighbourhood without a hub of its own hangs on the headend.
- A **ring** - a second way for the fibre, to another hub or separately to the headend - keeps a hub running when an excavator cuts its feeder; without it the whole neighbourhood is off until the splice crew is done.
- A **customer center** (a shop, *Cable customer center*) has the customer service and the devices. People of the neighbourhood come in while it is open: they look at the **device table** (Going Online's, from the furniture stores), sit down on the **waiting places** (the game's waiting room chairs, sofas or benches), watch the **television** - every TV there shows your company's spot - and go to a **customer desk** (Going Online's customer center workplace with someone on shift). New customers of the neighbourhood pick their devices up there - no parcel to pay for.

**Who serves how many:** a technician 400 customers, switching staff 800 coax customers, customer service 500 customers - each in the neighbourhood of their office or customer center. A network master leads up to 10 people in the field; beyond that they work slower. The Staff tab shows it per neighbourhood.

**Power and monitoring:** now and then the city's power fails in a neighbourhood. Batteries in the nodes' power supplies (Network tab, per neighbourhood) bridge two hours; a **UPS** keeps an office running for an hour, a **generator** as long as the cut lasts - without them a dark hub takes its neighbourhood down, the dark headend the whole city. The **network monitoring** (Network tab, a licence per day) finds faults before customers call, while a network master is on duty and a control room workplace stands in an office.

A provider from before Going Online 0.8 keeps the old rules for 10 days after the update.
